title: Issue 1 Cover — Between the Beacons
summary: Founding cover for Rex Fleet Academy: Between the Beacons. Sell the impossible ordinary road at the center of the issue: civilian life moves confidently through a measured green low-tension volume between beacons because survey, maintenance, certification and Fleet stewardship keep earning that trust. The corridor itself is the protagonist. Do not explain the lesson or reveal the later route-market, Shard, duty-watch, or Mirrorfold turns.
settingText: Deep space along a mature public corridor between two operational beacon stations. The camera is close enough to the near beacon to feel its industrial scale and looks down the certified route toward the second green beacon and a distant inhabited world. The public corridor is a real three-dimensional low-tension volume around a surveyed spine, not a hard tunnel: a soft translucent green envelope with a fine brighter measured spine, subtle physical gradient at the edge, and enough visible cross-section to understand that ships travel inside a volume. Ordinary civilian passenger and freight traffic occupies the green route. A blue-gold-white Fleet vessel protects the lane from outside the civilian stream; a purple survey craft works an offset pass beyond the certified envelope; a yellow maintenance tender is physically attached to the near beacon. No magical portal, no ocean channel walls, no generic neon highway.
panelPlan: Single full-bleed vertical comic cover. No interior panel grid, inset panels, collage, split-screen, dossier framing, or infographic layout.

ONE-SECOND SELLING IMAGE: an extraordinary green road through deep space that ordinary people trust enough to use like infrastructure. The near beacon, the luminous measured corridor volume, the civilian convoy, and the distant second beacon must form one immediately readable perspective chain.

Place the near beacon large in the lower foreground, partially cropped by the page edge so it feels like working infrastructure rather than a decorative icon. Its verified green status should be clear but restrained; the machinery itself remains Fleet-era industrial hardware rather than a giant glowing ring.

From that beacon, aim the corridor diagonally upward into depth toward the second green beacon and distant inhabited world. Show a fine surveyed spine inside a much wider soft circular safe envelope. The envelope has no hard walls. Its usable diameter should read as roughly twice the beam of the largest certified ship visible in the lane.

Inside the envelope, show a small number of ordinary civilian craft—a passenger vessel, working freighter, or mixed local traffic—with warm inhabited windows and practical cargo geometry. These ships are the human stake. They should look like people are simply going somewhere, not entering battle.

Keep the Fleet vessel blue/gold/Ion White and physically outside or above the civilian traffic stream, matching the route rather than visually owning it. Its role should read as protection/stewardship, not conquest.

Use one purple survey craft outside the certified envelope on a clearly offset measurement path and one yellow maintenance tender attached to the near beacon. They are secondary evidence that the road exists because people keep measuring and maintaining it, not a color-coded lineup.

Do not show Shard craft, a red public beacon, a leaked diagnostic, route brokers, the duty-watch medical-convoy crisis, the final green-restoration solution, or any Mirrorfold geometry. The cover asks why the road can be trusted; the issue gets to answer.

THUMBNAIL TEST: the green corridor perspective is the dominant shape; the two beacon points and civilian traffic remain legible when reduced; secondary survey/maintenance/Fleet roles enrich the image without becoming required tiny-detail reading.

TRADE-DRESS ZONE: preserve a clean upper band of Warp Black/deep star field, roughly the top quarter of the cover, with only restrained stars and the distant route perspective behind it. No ship silhouette, beacon machinery, or bright green bloom may destroy masthead legibility.

Founding masthead architecture should visibly belong to the released Rex Fleet family: large premium ivory/Ion-White block lettering with restrained gold edge/detail, dark-space breathing room, STAR SPLITTER VISIONS publisher lockup at upper left, and ISSUE #1 at upper right. Add ACADEMY as a clear sub-brand under/within the Rex Fleet masthead hierarchy, then make BETWEEN THE BEACONS the strong topic title. Do not copy the released Rex Fleet Issue 1 character montage or its three-way faction composition.

Color hierarchy: Warp Black/deep space field; green reserved for the verified public corridor/civilian continuity; blue/gold/Ion White for Fleet stewardship; purple survey; yellow maintenance. Avoid generic cyan neon, muddy AI beige, magical rainbow refraction, or bright-red Shard imagery on this founding cover.

directionInline.text: This is a single-image prestige science-fiction comic COVER, not an interior sequential page. Do not create a panel grid.

Required cover lettering is limited to the exact publisher/series trade dress: STAR SPLITTER VISIONS / REX FLEET / ACADEMY / BETWEEN THE BEACONS / ISSUE #1. No tagline, blurb, caption, character label, fake review quote, environmental signage, route label, HUD text, or other invented lettering.

Before generating this founding cover, retrieve and visually inspect the actual released Rex Fleet Issue 1 cover pixels from StarSplitterVisions at sites/visions/public/images/covers/rex-fleet-issue-01-green-corridor.jpg. Use those pixels only as parent-family guidance for premium Rex Fleet masthead weight, ivory/gold/black brand language, publisher-lockup placement logic, issue-number prominence, and overall cover finish. Do not copy its character montage, faction wedges, composition, story imagery, or exact palette distribution.

The corridor must obey established Between the Beacons physics: a measured three-dimensional low-tension volume around a surveyed spine with a soft physical edge, not a glowing tunnel with hard walls. Green means verified public route state; it is not Fleet faction color.
Judge the art at thumbnail size before accepting it. The cover must still read as 'ordinary ships trusting an impossible green road between two beacons' when small.

FOUNDING TRADE-DRESS COVER: after this exact cover is approved, persist the approved pixels to production/references/rex-fleet-academy-between-beacons/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.png and activate that asset in production/references/rex-fleet-academy-between-beacons/cover-production-normalization.json. Any later cover for this series must pixel-read that approved asset for masthead/trade-dress continuity before generation.

The approved Issue 1 cover controls later masthead identity, title hierarchy, issue-number treatment, margins, logo scale, and trade-dress geometry only. It must never force later issue-specific scene composition, cast, palette, lighting, camera angle, or story imagery.
